explanation: In Brazil, beckoning someone with your finger—especially with the palm facing up—is widely perceived as a rude, commanding gesture often associated with calling a dog or a servant. It conveys impatience and disrespect, and is avoided in everyday social and professional interactions. Brazilians typically use a more open-handed wave or a verbal call instead.
local_tip: To call someone politely, extend your hand with palm facing down and make a gentle scooping motion toward yourself, or simply say 'com licença' and wave discreetly.
regional_note: In some rural areas or among older generations, the gesture may be slightly less offensive, but it remains generally frowned upon nationwide.

also_check.note: Beckoning with the index finger is considered very rude, akin to calling an animal; use a hand wave with palm down instead.
Beckoning with a finger is highly offensive and can be interpreted as a challenge; use a gentle hand wave with palm down.
While common in casual settings, it can be seen as dismissive or condescending in formal or professional contexts.
